chapter_title_en: Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მონა მოვიდა, მიამბო ამბავი მე მართალია:
“თქვენსა ამბავსა იკითხავს აჯიღოსანი ქალია”.
მაშინვე ვიცან, ავიჭერ, ჩქარ-ჩქარად გულ-გამკრთალია;
და მოვიდა, ვნახე ასმათი, ჩემთანა მომავალია.
stanzas.english_translation: "She gave me a letter, I gazed on it; it was from the light of the face of the lands. She wrote: 'I have seen the loveliness of thy gemlike brilliancy; fair wert thou returned from battle, after urging on thy horse; not ill seems to me the cause of the flow of my tears.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 490; Wardrop Stanza 477): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე ვისთვის ვკვდები, მიამა ასმათის ნახვა მე მისად.
აღარ მივუშვი, ვაკოცე, ქმნადღა თაყვანის ცემისად;
ხელი მოვჰკიდე, დავისვი ახლოს ტახტისა ჩემისად,
და ვჰკითხე თუ: “ნეტარ მისულა მორჩი ალვისა ხე მისად?
stanzas.english_translation: "If God hath given me my tongue it befits me to use it for thy praise; dead for thy sake I can by no means speak, for lacking thee I die. The sun (i.e., Nestan) made a little garden of rose and jet, as a garden for the lion; by thy sun, my self pertains to none save thee.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 491; Wardrop Stanza 478): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მიამბე მისი ამბავი, სხვად ნურად მეუბნებია!”
მითხრა თუ: “გკადრებ ამბავსა, აწ ჩემგან არ სათნებია,
დღეს ერთმანერთი გინახავს და ტურფად მოგწონებია,
და აწ კვლაცა ცნობა ამბისა მას ჩემგან უბრძანებია”.
stanzas.english_translation: "'Though thou hast shed a stream of tears yet have they not flowed in vain; henceforth weep no more, put away grief from thee. Those who look upon thee curse unrestrained those who look upon thee. Veil me with that which but now was bound round thee.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 492; Wardrop Stanza 479): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“წიგნი მომართვა, ჩავხედენ, პირისა თემთა მთენისა.
ეწერა: “ვნახე სიტურფე წყალ-ჯავარისა შენისა.
ომ-გარდახდილი ჰშვენოდი, შენატევები ცხენისა,
და არ ავი მიჩანს მიზეზი ჩემისა ცრემლთა დენისა.
stanzas.english_translation: "'Give me the veils that sometime adorned thee; when thou seest me, thou also shalt be pleased that that which is thine adorns me. Bind on thine arm this bracelet if thou honourest what is mine, and such another night thou shalt not pass as long as thou livest.'"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 493; Wardrop Stanza 480): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.english_translation: Here Tariel, become like a wild beast, weeps, his grief increases a thousandfold; he said: "I have the armlet which she formerly bound on her arm!" He undid it, took it off, man cannot estimate its worth, he pressed it to his lips, he fainted and fell like a corpse.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 494; Wardrop Stanza 481): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“თუცა მიგდის ღვარი ცრემლთა, მაგრა ცუდად არ იდენო,
ამას იქით ნუღარა სტირ, ჭირსა თავი არიდენო;
შენნი მჭვრეტნი ჩემთა მჭვრეტთა აგინებენ, არ იდენო,
და რომე წეღან მოგეხვივნეს, იგი ჩემთვის არიდენო.
stanzas.english_translation: He lay more lifeless than a corpse at the door of the tomb. On both sides are seen bruises from his fist which he had struck on his breast. A stream of blood flows from Asmat’h's scratched cheeks; she poured water on him again, she succoured him, the sound of gurgling water is heard there.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 495; Wardrop Stanza 482): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil, too, sighed bitterly; he gazed on the unconscious form. Asmat’h multiplied her groans; her tears hollowed out the stones. Then she restored him to consciousness, his fires she quenched with water; he said: "I live; Fate even now is drinking my blood."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 20 ('Letter of Nestan-Darejan to her Beloved', Stanza 496; Wardrop Stanza 483): Part of the narrative sequence in which nestan-Darejan sends Tariel a jewelled armlet to bind on his arm and asks for the Khatavian veil he wore at the banquet so she may wear it in remembrance of him.

key_maxim_ka: გველსა ხვრელით ამოიყვანს ენა ტკბილად მოუბარი
key_maxim_en: A sweetly speaking tongue brings a snake out from its lair.
